deep.reconstruction:
Context: the facing printed page (p.105 of a textbook) explains how to improve an approximate root of x = w^m. Gauss's notes on this blank verso concern a different route to square roots: periodic continued fractions and periodic linear recurrences, treated through what is in effect the trace and determinant of 2x2 matrices.

(1) 'Comp.' = composition. Take two quadratics x^2 - a x - b and x^2 - a' x - b'. Each is the characteristic polynomial of a one-step block of the recurrence y_{k+1} = a y_k + b y_{k-1}, i.e. of the matrix M = [[a,1],[b,0]]. If the coefficients alternate (a,b), (a',b'), then the two-step block M M' = [[aa'+b', a],[a'b, b]] governs every second term. Its trace is aa'+b+b' and its determinant is bb'. Gauss writes the 'composite' pair as (aa'+b+b', -bb') in the same x^2 - A x - B format. He then writes the composite quadratic x^2 - (aa'+b+b')x + bb' = (x-e)(x-f), with roots e and f.

(2) The three-column table gives the solution of the alternating recurrence. The even-indexed terms are x_{2m} = t e^m + u f^m. The page appears to read u e^n; this is probably u f^m (my reading). The odd-indexed terms are ((e-b)/a) t e^m + ... (only the t-part is written). The next even term is t e^{m+1} + u f^{m+1}.
Check (mine): if x_{2m} = t e^m and x_{2m+2} = a x_{2m+1} + b x_{2m}, then t e^{m+1} = a s e^m + b t e^m. This gives s = (e-b)t/a, exactly the middle entry.

(3) The column a', a'', a''' with 1's beside them indicates partial quotients with partial numerators 1, over a period of length 3.

(4) A first attempt, ap+b=pq, bq+c, is crossed out. It is replaced by ap+1=pq, bq+1=qr, cr+1=rp, i.e. q = a+1/p, r = b+1/q, p = c+1/r. So p = c + 1/(b + 1/(a + 1/p)) is a purely periodic continued fraction of period 3, and p, q, r are its complete quotients.

(5) The last line, 'abcP = p^2 -', breaks off. The most plausible completion (mine) takes P = pqr, the product of the complete quotients over one period.
- Since [[a_i,1],[1,0]](x_{i+1},1)^T = x_{i+1}(x_i,1)^T, P is an eigenvalue of the period matrix [[c,1],[1,0]][[b,1],[1,0]][[a,1],[1,0]].
- That matrix has trace abc+a+b+c and determinant (-1)^3 = -1.
- Hence P^2 - (abc+a+b+c)P - 1 = 0, i.e. abcP = P^2 - (a+b+c)P - 1. This fits the visible beginning.
- Eliminating q and r directly gives the quadratic for p itself: (ab+1)p^2 - (abc+a+c-b)p - (bc+1) = 0.

(6) Application: 'So findet man z. B. sqrt30 = 5.4772255667...' and sqrt3 = 1.73205.
- sqrt30 = [5; 2, 10] has period 2. Composing (2,1) with (10,1) gives x^2 - 22x + 1, whose roots are 11 ± 2 sqrt30.
- sqrt3 = [1; 1, 2], period 2.
- The method thus yields high-accuracy square roots, offered as an alternative to the textbook's Newton/Halley-type correction on the facing page.
errors: The decimal written for sqrt30 is not quite right. The true value is 5.4772255750516...; the page shows roughly 5.4772255667 (with a correction digit 7 written above). The error is in the 8th decimal place. It may come from a convergent, e.g. 5291/966 = 5.47722567... or 55435/10121 = 5.47722557..., or from a copying slip.
The line 'abcP = p^2 -' is unfinished. The variable may be P = pqr rather than p, and no complete equation is given.
The second exponent written as u e^n should presumably be u f^m (second root), unless n is deliberate. As written it is ambiguous.
No errors in the composition formula: trace aa'+b+b' and determinant bb' are correct.
No errors in the middle-column coefficient (e-b)t/a.

results.what: Composition of two quadratics x^2-ax-b, x^2-a'x-b' into x^2-(aa'+b+b')x+bb' (characteristic polynomial of the product of the matrices [[a,1],[b,0]] and [[a',1],[b',0]])
results.modern_name: Matrix (trace/determinant) formulation of continued fractions / periodic second-order linear recurrences
results.usually_credited_to: Euler and Lagrange (continuants, periodic continued fractions); matrix form standard in the 19th-20th century

results.what: Closed form of an alternating-coefficient recurrence: even terms t e^m + u f^m, odd terms ((e-b)/a) t e^m + ...
results.modern_name: Solution of a linear recurrence with periodic coefficients via the monodromy (period) matrix

results.what: Period-3 purely periodic continued fraction written as the cyclic system ap+1=pq, bq+1=qr, cr+1=rp, with (apparently) the product of complete quotients P=pqr satisfying P^2-(abc+a+b+c)P-1=0
results.modern_name: Product of the complete quotients over a period equals the eigenvalue (unit) of the period matrix; purely periodic continued fractions are reduced quadratic irrationals
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange (1770), Galois (1829, purely periodic case); Gauss's Disquisitiones treats periods of reduced forms

results.what: Numerical square roots (sqrt30, sqrt3) via periodic continued fractions
results.modern_name: Continued fraction approximation of square roots

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard scratch computations on periodic continued fractions and recurrences, in effect 2x2 matrix trace and determinant. The material was well known from Euler and Lagrange and is closely tied to Gauss's own published theory of periods of reduced forms. The implicit matrix composition is a nice touch but not new.
